text:
ira-support: Hey team, customer (acme-corp) reports SSO failures after IdP rotated cert. SP is rejecting SAMLResponse signature. Happening since ~08:20 UTC.

alex: Can you paste the verification error/logs and the IdP metadata they uploaded?

ira-support: Pasting relevant shard of the auth log: ```
ERROR sso.verify SignatureValidationError: signature referenced key not found (thumbprint mismatch)
  at verifySignedAssertion (/srv/auth/sso/verify.js:112)
  at processAssertion (/srv/auth/sso/handler.js:48)
```
Also noticed ACS mismatch in our logs: incoming request has ACS `/sso/app%2Fcallback` encoded, our config expects `/sso/app/callback`.

oncall-bot: incident-created #sso-2203 (priority P2) — assigned to eng-saml. :rotating_light:

maya: Two things to check quickly: 1) IdP metadata may be signed with the old key (thumbprint mismatch) or the <KeyDescriptor use="signing"> ordering changed. 2) URL encoding/normalization — our SP normalizes decoded ACS paths, but some IdPs sign the original encoded URL which changes the signed value.

jordan: Do we have the uploaded metadata XML from the customer? If they uploaded a metadata bundle right after rotation it's possible the metadata still references the old cert in ds:Signature.

ira-support: Uploaded file attached by customer (metadata.xml). Snippet: ```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme-corp.com">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>
        <X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...OLDCERT...==</X509Certificate></X509Data>
      </KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>
        <X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...NEWCERT...==</X509Certificate></X509Data>
      </KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
They uploaded both keys but signature block references the OLDCERT.

maya: That explains thumbprint mismatch. Two options: ask IdP to re-sign metadata (or the Assertion) with the new key, or configure our SP to accept dual-key metadata where we search KeyDescriptor list rather than only first matching cert. Short-term we can accept the old thumbprint if customer confirms the old cert is still valid but they rotated it — risky.

alex: Also need to address ACS URL encoding. Ask customer to ensure the Assertion Consumer Service URL in the signed Assertion exactly matches the ACS URL we have (percent-encoding matters). Provide repro command: 
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://sp.redwood.example/sso/saml/acs -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-urlencode 'SAMLResponse=<base64-assertion>'
```
If the IdP signs the encoded URL, signing verification may fail on our side if we normalize before checking.

ira-support: Customer says their IdP (on-prem SAML appliance) recently toggled a setting to canonicalize URLs. They also rotated certs last night.

eng-saml: Assigning eng-saml to investigate. Short repro steps for us: 1) load their metadata.xml into a local test SP (python3 -m http.server + saml-tooling) 2) replay a captured SAMLResponse from their debug logs (we already have one). 3) verify signature using xmlsec with both certs.

maya: Quick diagnostic command: ```bash
# verify signature against both certs
xmlsec1 --verify --enabled-key-data x509 --pubkey-cert-der oldcert.der assertion.xml || xmlsec1 --verify --enabled-key-data x509 --pubkey-cert-der newcert.der assertion.xml
```
If oldcert succeeds but newcert fails, the Assertion was still signed with the old key.

eng-saml: Also checking our SSO metadata cache — metadata fetcher caches remote IdP metadata for 5m by default, and we have a queued metadata refresh job. If customer uploaded new metadata via console it can take up to 30s to propagate to all SP nodes. Suggest clearing the cache for the tenant: `POST /admin/tenants/{id}/sso/clear-metadata-cache` (internal API).

jordan: Customer asked what to do now. Suggested message to send them: "Please confirm whether the IdP is signing SAML Assertions with the new cert. If they rotated keys, ensure the assertion signature and the metadata signature both reference the same certificate. Also check the ACS URL in the signed Assertion matches exactly (including percent-encoding) our configured ACS: https://app.redwood.example/sso/app/callback. If they can't re-sign, upload metadata signed with the new cert and retry."

ira-support: Customer replied: they re-signed assertions but still getting signature errors. They uploaded a re-signed assertion trace. Provided base64 assertion for us to verify.

maya: I ran the xmlsec verification against the re-signed assertion — signature still references oldcert. Looks like their IdP didn't actually switch the signing key for assertions, only for metadata. I'll open a coordination thread with their IdP admin.

eng-saml: Mitigation plan: 1) Ask IdP to reconfigure assertion signing to use the new key. 2) We can temporarily accept the old thumbprint for that tenant while they fix IdP (risk accepted by customer). 3) Add a short-term enhancement to our SP: check KeyDescriptor list when verifying signatures (won't land immediately).

alex: I'll send the mitigation options and the exact admin API call to clear metadata cache to the customer. Also scheduling a short sync with their IdP ops.

ira-support: Customer confirmed they want the temporary thumbprint acceptance while they fix IdP. They provided contact for IdP admin. Moving to escalate to a P2 support handoff.

oncall-bot: pager-duty note — eng-saml on-call acknowledged. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Marking this thread resolved once customer confirms successful login after the IdP fixes signing. Will follow up in 2 hours. :thumbsup:
